HS19 vs. HS2: Variant Calling Under NaOCl Selection

A joint-genotyped, quality-filtered survey of SNPs, indels, and structural variants in a hypochlorite-adapted mutant line
Prepared 2026-07-23 · Reference: HS2_polished.fa (HiFi de novo assembly, 66.6 Mb) · Short-read Illumina WGS, HS19 vs. HS2-self

Part One — Findings

Executive summary

HS19 is a Chlorella sp. HS2-derived mutant line selected under sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl) exposure — a fundamentally different selective pressure from the hydrolysate-adapted ALE line studied elsewhere in this project. This report presents a rerun of HS19's variant calling using the same rigorous joint-genotyping framework validated for ALE, against the same high-quality HS2 HiFi reference assembly.

Mean HS19 read depth

The honest headline is mixed: the SNP/indel calling is methodologically solid and yields a defensible set of 263 high-confidence HS19-specific variants, 57 of which fall in coding regions with HIGH or MODERATE predicted impact. But the search for NaOCl-relevant candidate genes returned no strong, specific hits — none of the core oxidative/chlorine-stress gene categories (catalase, superoxide dismutase, glutathione system, heat-shock proteins, ABC efflux transporters, photosystem-II D1 repair) appear among the confidently-called, high-impact HS19-specific mutations. This is reported as a genuine negative result, not smoothed over.

Selection pressure & framing

HS19's defining selective pressure was NaOCl (sodium hypochlorite / bleach) treatment — an oxidative and chlorinating stress that primarily damages proteins, membranes, and DNA through reactive chlorine/oxygen species. This is mechanistically distinct from ALE's hydrolysate-derived stress (furanic compounds, organic acids, osmotic/salinity stress) discussed in the companion HS2×ALE report. The two mutant lines are analyzed independently throughout this project and should not be conflated: shared infrastructure (the HS2 reference genome, the snpEff annotation database, the QC filter design) does not imply shared biology.

Candidate functional categories considered Oxidative/chlorine-radical detoxification (catalase, SOD, glutathione system, peroxiredoxin, thioredoxin) · DNA repair (glycosylases, mismatch repair, recombinases) · Chaperones/heat-shock proteins · Membrane and cell-wall remodeling · Efflux/ABC transporters · Photosystem II D1 repair machinery.

Key statistics

SNVs and indels

Joint genotyping of HS19 and an HS2-self short-read control against the HS2 HiFi reference produced 7,950 total variant records across both samples. Restricting to sites where HS2-self is confidently homozygous-reference and HS19 carries a non-reference, non-missing genotype isolates 752 raw HS19-specific candidates (238 SNPs, 514 indels).

The indel-heavy skew (241 of 263 PASS variants) is expected given GATK's well-documented weaker indel-calling performance relative to DeepVariant, compounded by the absence of base-quality score recalibration (no known-sites VCF exists for this non-model organism). Four independent frameshift indels recur at the SURF1 locus window across widely separated positions on the same contig (ptg000012l) — worth a second look for whether this reflects a genuinely repeat-rich/mutation-prone region, an assembly/annotation artifact (broad transcript windows), or, less likely given the spacing, four independent real mutations in one gene neighborhood.

NaOCl candidate-gene search

Every PASS/FLAGGED HS19-specific variant's associated gene name, snpEff effect, and GO/KEGG annotation was searched against the six NaOCl-relevant functional categories defined in Selection pressure & framing. The result is a clear negative for five of six categories:

CategoryAny hit (n=462)PASS + HIGH/MODERATE (n=263)
Oxidative / chlorine detox (catalase, SOD, glutathione system, peroxiredoxin, thioredoxin)00
DNA repair10
Chaperone / heat-shock protein00
Efflux / ABC transporter (xenobiotic)00
Photosystem II D1 repair00
Membrane / cell wall8512
Read this result carefully, not optimistically The only category with hits is "membrane," matched via the generic substring "membrane" against GO/UniProt annotation text — this term appears in hundreds of unrelated GO annotations (plasma membrane, mitochondrial membrane, membrane transport, etc.) and is not a specific signature of NaOCl-driven membrane remodeling. None of the 12 strict hits carry a GO term more specific than a bare "membrane" mention. We do not present this as evidence of an oxidative-stress mechanism — it is reported because the search was pre-registered as part of this analysis, not because the result supports the hypothesis.

Three honest interpretations are possible, and this report does not adjudicate between them: (1) HS19's true causal mutations exist but sit in genes whose functional annotation is incomplete or too generic in the current HS2 GO/KEGG crosswalk to be caught by keyword search; (2) the causal mutations are regulatory/non-coding and invisible to a coding-impact-weighted search; (3) NaOCl adaptation in this strain may act more through non-genetic (epigenetic, physiological, or population-heterogeneity) mechanisms than through the specific coding mutations captured here. Distinguishing between these would require either deeper manual literature curation of the 291 named genes among all candidates, or complementary expression data.

Structural variants

Delly (v0.8.3) was run independently on HS19 and an HS2-self control, then HS19 calls were compared against HS2-self by position and type (±500 bp tolerance) to isolate HS19-specific candidates.

192
HS19 PASS SV calls (raw)
2,927
HS2-self PASS SV calls (background)
13
HS19-specific, non-inversion (confident)
164
HS19-specific inversions (low-confidence)
A large, likely-artifactual background HS2-self showed nearly 15× more PASS SV calls than HS19 despite only ~1.4× higher read depth (115× vs. 80.6×) — and both sets are dominated (86–96%) by the inversion (INV) category. Inspection shows these INV calls have a suspicious signature: QUAL is a near-perfect deterministic function of split-read count alone (QUAL = SR × 60, e.g. SR=3 → QUAL=180) with zero paired-end support, across hundreds of unrelated genomic positions. This is a recognized failure mode of short-read split-read-based inversion calling — not a validated biological signal. The likely technical driver is HS2_vs_polished.merged.bam combining multiple sequencing runs/libraries with inconsistent insert-size characteristics, which inflates spurious discordant/split-read signals.

Excluding inversions, HS19-specific candidates are: 7 deletions, 5 breakends, 1 duplication. These are more plausible but still single-caller, short-read-only calls with no long-read or second-caller cross-validation (unlike ALE's pbsv+Sniffles2+assembly-alignment triangulation) — treat as candidates for follow-up validation (e.g., PCR/Sanger across the breakpoint, or targeted long-read sequencing), not confirmed structural mutations.

Comparison to prior analysis

BioTo's 2025-09-11 report analyzed the same HS19-vs-HS2 comparison using a ~52 Mb/52-scaffold filtered subset of the seeders.co.kr assembly (vs. our complete 66.6 Mb HiFi assembly) and SAMtools v0.1.16 (a 2011-era caller). Two points of agreement and one point of caution:

  • Agreement — SV calling. BioTo used three short-read SV callers (BreakDancer, Pindel, Delly) and found zero SVs confirmed by all three; their own manual IGV review concluded no convincing SV signal was present. Our independent Delly-based analysis, run fresh on our own mapping, similarly found the bulk of raw SV signal attributable to a known-unreliable call class (short-read inversions), leaving only a small residual candidate set. Two independent analyses, different reference and toolchains, arriving at the same cautious conclusion is a meaningful cross-check.
  • Caution — SNP calling. BioTo reported 3,462 total SNPs with 3,426 (99%) classified heterozygous. Given this project's own finding that HS2's true heterozygosity is roughly 0.0036% (see the companion HS2×ALE report), a 99% heterozygous call rate is very likely an artifact of their older caller rather than real biology. We do not treat their raw SNP count as a target our own numbers should match.
  • Mapping quality. HS19 reads mapped to our complete reference at 97.89%, exceeding BioTo's own 93.18% against their smaller reference — independent evidence that the fuller HiFi assembly is the better substrate for this analysis.

Limitations

There is no error-free option here This analysis follows the same joint-genotyping framework validated for ALE specifically to avoid the false-positive inflation from independent-sample calling. But HS19 has short-read data only — no long-read HS19 assembly exists to cross-validate against, unlike ALE, which had HiFi long reads as primary evidence plus short-read cross-validation. HS19's results therefore sit at a lower achievable confidence ceiling than ALE's, regardless of how carefully the short-read calling is done. Readers should not treat the two strains' results as equally weighted evidence.
  • No base-quality score recalibration (BQSR) — no known-sites VCF exists for this non-model organism, a standard limitation, not unique to this analysis.
  • GATK's default hard-filter thresholds are tuned on human WGS characteristics and have not been empirically recalibrated against this genome's quality-score distribution.
  • GATK is known to underperform DeepVariant specifically on indel-calling benchmarks — consistent with the indel-heavy, lower-precision profile seen here relative to ALE's DeepVariant-based calls.
  • The NaOCl candidate-gene search is a keyword-based screen against existing GO/KEGG annotation, not a functional/expression-based test — a true negative here does not rule out causal genes with incomplete annotation.
  • SV calling used a single caller (Delly) with no long-read or second-caller confirmation for HS19, unlike ALE's three-way triangulation.

Part Two — Methods

Pipeline overview

This pipeline reuses the shared HS2 project infrastructure (the HiFi de novo reference assembly, the chlorella_hs2_v2 snpEff database, and the Trinity/Trinotate-derived gene/GO/KEGG annotation tables) built for the HS2×ALE comparison, applied fresh to HS19's own short-read data.

1 Read trimming (fastp) and mapping (bwa mem) onto HS2_polished.fa
2 MarkDuplicates on both HS19 and an HS2-self short-read control
3 GATK HaplotypeCaller (GVCF mode, diploid) for both samples independently
4 CombineGVCFs + GenotypeGVCFs — joint genotyping across both samples
5 Extraction of HS19-specific sites (HS2-self hom-ref, HS19 non-ref)
6 Density filter (±500 bp clustering) and coverage/contig-edge QC filter
7 snpEff annotation + gene/GO/KEGG merge
8 Delly SV calling on both samples, overlap-based subtraction
9 Combined mutation map and summary figures

Read mapping

HS19 raw paired-end reads (45M read pairs, 151 bp, ~1.48–1.52 GB per mate) were trimmed with fastp and mapped onto the 66.6 Mb HS2 HiFi reference (HS2_polished.fa) with bwa mem. Result: 97.89% primary mapping rate, 97.03% properly paired, 83.5× genome-wide mean depth. The pre-existing HS2-self short-read BAM (from the earlier HS2×ALE short-read cross-validation work, 115.1× mean depth) was reused directly as the joint-genotyping control rather than remapped.

Joint genotyping

Both samples were called with gatk HaplotypeCaller -ERC GVCF --sample-ploidy 2, combined with CombineGVCFs, and jointly genotyped with GenotypeGVCFs. This is the same fix applied to the ALE pipeline after naive single-sample calling inflated variant counts by misreading HS2's own repeat-complexity noise as sample-specific differences (28,611/3,931 variants before the fix). Joint genotyping calls both samples against the same evidence model simultaneously, so a site is only reported as HS19-specific if HS19's genotype is confidently different from HS2-self's at that same site — not because each caller happened to sample the site differently.

HS19-specific extraction: bcftools view -i 'GT[1]="RR" && GT[0]!="RR" && GT[0]!="mis"' (HS2-self homozygous reference, HS19 non-reference and called).

Filtering

Density filter

Any candidate within 500 bp of another candidate on the same contig was flagged as clustered and removed (290 of 752 raw candidates) — dense local clusters are a recognized signature of misalignment around indels/repeats rather than independent mutation events, the same threshold used for ALE.

Coverage / contig-edge QC filter

For each remaining candidate: local read depth was computed in an 11 bp window; a variant was flagged if local depth < 20× (absolute), local depth < 25% of the contig's mean depth (relative), or the variant sat within 1,000 bp of a contig edge. This mirrors the identical filter used and validated on the ALE dataset.

Annotation

PASS+density-filtered variants were annotated with snpEff against the existing chlorella_hs2_v2 database (unchanged since it is built directly on HS2_polished.fa — no rebuild needed). Gene names, UniProt IDs, and GO/KEGG terms were joined via the existing locus-coordinate window lookup and UniProt crosswalk tables built for the ALE analysis.

SV calling

delly call (v0.8.3) was run independently against HS19.dedup.bam and HS2_self.dedup.bam. PASS calls from each were compared by chromosome, SV type, and position/end (±500 bp tolerance); HS19 calls with no matching HS2-self call were retained as HS19-specific candidates. Delly was chosen specifically because it is short-read compatible and was one of the three callers in BioTo's original analysis, enabling direct methodological comparability.

Caller tradeoffs

GATK HaplotypeCaller was used in place of DeepVariant (the caller used for ALE) after repeated Docker/WSL integration failures made DeepVariant infeasible to run reliably in this environment. Known tradeoffs, stated transparently:

  • No BQSR possible (no known-sites VCF for this species) — a standard non-model-organism limitation, not unique to this choice.
  • GATK's default hard-filter thresholds are tuned on human WGS quality-score distributions and were not empirically recalibrated here.
  • GATK generally underperforms DeepVariant on indel-calling benchmarks specifically, in published caller comparisons.

None of these are disqualifying for the purposes of this survey-level analysis, but they set the confidence ceiling below what ALE's DeepVariant-based calls achieved.

Reproducibility

All scripts referenced in this report live under ~/genomics/chlorella_hifi/scripts/ (WSL): hs19_trim_map.sh, hs19_gatk_pipeline.sh, hs19_density_filter.py, hs19_qc_filter.py, hs19_build_merged_table.py, hs19_naocl_search_run.py, hs19_sv_specific.py, hs19_mutation_map.py. Intermediate and final data tables live under ~/genomics/chlorella_hifi/variants/hs19/.
